title: Factory: build the right object from a name
summary: One method turns a name into the right object, so the rest of the code never has to know which classes exist.

say.never: At a pizza shop, you say "pepperoni" and a pizza comes out. You don't go into the kitchen and pick the ingredients. A **factory** is a method like that kitchen: you hand it a name, and it builds the right object and hands it back. Its return type is an interface, so the caller only knows "I got a pizza", not which class it was. Each call builds a fresh one with `new`.
say.bit: **Factory**: a method takes a name and returns a new object of the right class, typed as the interface.

say.never: People type names in all sorts of ways: `"Pepperoni"`, `"PEPPERONI"`, `" pepperoni "`. Tidy the name before you match it. `trim()` cuts spaces off both ends, and `toLowerCase()` makes every letter small. Both give back a *new* string, so use what they return. And watch out for `null`: calling a method on `null` crashes, so check for it first.
say.bit: `trim()` and `toLowerCase()` tidy the name (they return a new string). Check `null` before calling either.

steps.title: In your lesson: Tidy the name first

say.never: `AutoFactory.create(name)` turns the dashboard's choice into an `Auto`. Handle `null` first, then tidy the name and match it against the four names in the comment. Anything else gets a `DoNothingAuto`, the safe choice. Every match builds a new object, and nothing ever returns `null`.
say.bit: `create`: null check, tidy, match four names, `DoNothingAuto` for anything else. Always `new`, never `null`.

say.never: Hold down **Ctrl** and tap **P**. A small search box pops up at the top. Type `AutoFactory`, then press **Enter**. It finds any file by its name, so you never have to dig through folders.

It may be further down. Click in the code, then hold **Ctrl** and tap **F** to open the search box. Type `public static Auto create(String name)` and press **Enter**. The editor scrolls to the right spot and highlights it.
say.bit: Press **Ctrl+F**, type `public static Auto create(String name)` and press Enter to jump to it.

waitFor.hint: find public static Auto create(String name) with Ctrl+F.

say.never: Your turn! Write `create`. A `switch` on the tidied name works well, or a chain of `if` and `.equals(...)`. (Don't compare strings with `==`.)
